in patients with systolic heart failure and mild to moderate anaemia, circulating levels of the monocyte/macrophages markers sCD163 and MIF, and T-cell markers sIL-2r and ALCAM, are associated with adverse outcome and may reflect a systemic inflammatory response in these patients, however, the association was lost after adjustment for established biomarkers of cardiac damage and dysfunction.

leukocyte activation markers sIL-2, ALCAM, sCD163, and MIF were independently associated with adverse outcome but did not add prognostic information on top of established risk markers in patients with HfrEF and mild to moderate anaemia.

circulating levels of sCD163, ALCAM, MIF, and sIL-2 receptor were associated with adverse outcomes in patients with systolic heart failure and mild to moderate degree of anemia, but the prognostic value of these markers was limited when added to the prognostic models including the established biomarkers NT-proBNP and cardiac troponin T. A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the circulating markers of T-cell and monocyte/macropahge activation, which were associated with adverse outcomes in univariate and multivariable analyses, were not independent predictors of outcome in patients with HF with reduced ejection fractions (HFREF) and mild to moderate anaemia, after adjustment for established biomarkers of cardiac injury and inflammation.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the circulating levels of the leukocyte activation markers sIL2R, ALCAM, MIF and sCD163 were associated with worse outcomes in anemic patients, but did not add prognostic value on top of established biomarkers such as TnT and BNP.
